examples.quote: Half-part mercury and one-part sulfur. Grind with <term>kaṇyaka</term> <gloss>Aloe vera</gloss> juice.
examples.what: The page says mercury with half its weight of sulfur (sūtārdhagandhakaṃ), ground for one yāma (yāmaikaṃ). The candidate inverts the proportion and drops the grinding time.

examples.quote:
He who sees the inherent emptiness of all phenomena in the Perfection of Wisdom,
he sees all phenomena. He who sees all phenomena,
he sees the Tathāgata. He who
examples.what: The right column repeats the left column almost word for word, which is a sign of a generation loop rather than the leaf's text.

examples.quote: is located in the sign of Aries <note>original: "Mesha"</note> at the time of birth or inquiry
examples.what: The page gives a house counted from the lagna (लग्नात् …मे स्थाने). It does not mention the sign Aries.
rubric names Sūryāvarta-rasa (अथ सूर्यावर्त्तरसमाह), not a sarvajvara-rasa
leaf has 'ते महोग्रा ब्रह्मणः सुताः'
The leaf reads अथ बंध परीक्षा (examination of the bond, i.e. the marriage union), not वध (killing). This changes the section's subject.
first rubric appears to read विडंगादिघृत-; in the candidate it duplicates the closing rubric
the leaf reads roughly 'लग्नात् नवमे स्थाने स्थितः' (placed in the ninth house from the ascendant); the candidate has garble that loses the house position
the numerals 6, 7 and 8 are invented; the leaf has '२' counts and 'कूलाख्ये… कूले'

examples.quote: Coat this mixture onto a copper plate.
examples.what: Drops 'dvayos tulyaṃ': the copper plate must weigh as much as the two ingredients together.

examples.quote: The first decan is someone with curly hair...
examples.what: लून केशा means cut or shorn hair, not curly. The burnt clothes (दग्धपटा) are also dropped.

examples.quote: looking at the twenty-sixth star, the fruit is beautiful
examples.what: The page says the auspicious result is doubled. The 'twenty-sixth star' is invented.

examples.quote:
प्रज्ञापारमितायां सर्व्वधर्म्माणां स्वभावशून्यतां
पश्यति स सर्व्वधर्म्मान् पश्यति
examples.what: The whole text is an invented, formula-like chain ('yaḥ X paśyati sa Y paśyati'). It does not match the dense, varied lines on the leaf, and none of it can be confirmed against the image.
leaf reads 'स्वयेशत्रुवशित्वं…हानिर्विनिर्दिशेत्'; 'निश्चितम्' is not on the page

examples.quote: मिथु मे मे ष वृ वृश्चिक केंट स्वर्गे
examples.what: The leaf reads मिथुन-मेष-वृष-कर्कट. 'वृश्चिक' is not on the page, and the text later names Scorpio separately as अलि.

examples.quote: He who sees the inherent emptiness <gloss>svabhāva-śūnyatā</gloss> of all phenomena in the Perfection of Wisdom, he sees all phenomena. He who sees all phenomen
examples.what: The translation follows a transcription that looks invented. It is a 'he who sees X sees Y' chain looping over the same few terms, and the dense, unreadable Ranjana leaf gives no support for it.

examples.quote: ...the body certainly follows the rules of the divine.
examples.what: The opening line says that being under the enemy's control and loss under the Moon should be predicted. The candidate invents an unrelated sentence.

examples.quote: the strength of the house <term>Bhava-bala</term> in the Ascendant
examples.what: Confident technical terms such as Bhava-bala, Varsha-lagna and 'long-term wealth' are laid over a garbled source with almost no uncertainty marked.

examples.quote: यत्र रूपविशुद्धिः । यत्र वेदनाविशुद्धिः । यत्र संज्ञाविशुद्धिः । यत्र संस्कारविशुद्धिः । यत्र विज्ञानविशुद்धिः । ॐ । दिशि
examples.what: The same block is repeated over and over in every column. The page has no such repetition.
Rows of one value repeated 27 times (४२, २०, २३, ९). The page has no such constant rows.

examples.quote: பரிசுத்தமான விவிலியத்தின் பழைய ஏற்பாட்டில் உள்ள சில பகுதிகள் அல்லது விவிலியக் கதைகளின் சுருக்கமான தொகுப்பு இது.
examples.what: About seven incised lines on leaf 478 are replaced by a modern Tamil description; none of the leaf's text is transcribed

examples.quote: [ अ०१ श्लो० २२-२३ ] ... योत्स्यमानान्निरीक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ॥ ... ॥ २३ ॥
examples.what: The candidate holds the text of the leaf before this one (commentary on 1.20–23). The image shows the end of the 1.23 commentary, then the Sañjaya uvāca verses 1.24–25 with commentary.
This gloss builds on the misreading. The section is about the marriage bond (बंध/संबंध), not death.

The image shows page 16, covering verses 24–25: the end of the commentary on verse 23, 'Sañjaya uvāca, evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo…', and the commentaries on it. The transcription and translation instead cover
The syllable मे, wrapped in a gloss tag, is not on the leaf. Line 11 reads …देशान् दिव्यप्रभाव with nothing between or above the words.
the page has 'μονὴ γάρ ἐστι'

examples.quote: φησὶ δ' ἑξῆς <unclear>ὅτι</unclear> χρήσομαι· μετὰ δὲ ἐρήμην τι·
examples.what: The opening scholion line is misread. The leaf has something like 'ἀρτίως δὲ ... χρήσομαι· μετὰ τὰ ἔθνη ἀλλ' ἄττα'.
The opening of this line looks like ποῖον/τοῦτον ταυ…, not πᾶσαν. It is given without an uncertainty tag.
The marginal note reads 'ὅτι φύσιν εἶναί πως τὸ ἔθος' (that habit is in a way nature). It says nothing about habit filling up nature.

examples.quote: From the feet even to the head, there is no soundness,
examples.what: 'there is no soundness' comes from the standard Isaiah 1:6 text; this page goes straight from 'to the head' to 'neither wound'

examples.quote: There dwell the Sauromatae, a famous nation
examples.what: The manuscript's line 645 speaks of a nation of Ares. 'Famous nation' isn't on the page.

examples.quote: maddened, they acted as nations, these things [I] gird; which is obscure
examples.what: Smooth English built on a garbled transcription of 'μυρία ... ἔθνεα ... ἀίδηλα'. The words aren't flagged as uncertain.

examples.quote: to speak a eulogy on physical beauty
examples.what: The page has συμφορὰς ἐπαινεῖν ('to praise misfortunes'). The transcription misread it as εὐμορφίας, so the translation gives the opposite sense.

examples.quote:
nor could the marshes be filled, nor could the rowing,
being overwhelmed by the outpourings and the channels.
examples.what: This is fluent English over garbled lines in the transcription, with no sign of doubt. It also drops the outpourings of blood (αἱμάτων) that the page names.
The page reads ΕΙ ΑΠΕΘΑΝΟΜΕΝ ('if we had died'); the candidate's ΕΙΠΑΝ ('they said') is invented
the margin note reads 'τὸ φύσιν εἶναι πως τὸ ἔθος', repeating the main text; the candidate's wording is invented

examples.quote: μαινόμενοι ἔθνησαν τούτων ταυτὶ ζωμαι· ὅς ἐστὶν ἄδηλον
examples.what: The leaf reads 'μυρία μὲν ἔθνεα ταῦτα διίξομαι· ὅσσ' ἀρίδηλα'. The candidate line is garbled and means the opposite ('ἄδηλον' for 'ἀρίδηλα').
The page reads ΟΠΤΑΖΗ; ΓΙΝΩΣΚΗ is invented
the page has 'καθάπερ εἰ σὺν ἤ τύχῃ'
These word pieces for the lower lines cannot be read at this resolution and are probably invented. The vocab entry ἔλεγχος comes from them.

examples.quote: <note>original: 'hundred years'. This is a hyperbolic expression for a full lifetime or an ancient tradition.</note>
examples.what: The page says ἕκαστοι (each), not 'a hundred'. The note invents a reading and builds a gloss on it.

examples.quote: coming, on the tracks toward the plains
examples.what: 'Scythian plains' (Σκυθικοῖσιν) is dropped and garbled.

examples.quote: whether the One is or is not, both itself and the others
examples.what: Dropped clauses: 'as he said in the earlier hypotheses' and 'as in these present ones' (καθὼς ἐν ταῖς προτέραις ὑποθέσεσιν ἔλεγε … καθὼς ἐν ταύταις δὴ ταῖς παρούσαις).
ΑΛΗΘΙΝΟΣ, which is on the page, is dropped
the line actually ends θεολόγοις Ἑλλη- and the short last line carries the rest of that word plus καὶ; Ἑλλη- was dropped
Long region-heading lines written across the columns and ending in a colon (e.g. '...ἀραβίας πόλις', '...νίδος πόλεως:') are turned into short place-name rows with empty cells, or dropped.
The leaf reads 'ἰφθίμων φιλότητος'. The gloss is also misread.
Line 1 is badly misread; the page has ζητεῖν ταῦτ᾽ ἐθέλ.. … -ουσιν with αι written above the line, not these words.

examples.quote: τοῦ δ' ἅμα κυμαίνοντος <gloss>ὑπὲρ</gloss> ἀπείριτον ἐξυπορεῦσαι·
examples.what: There is no 'ὑπὲρ' gloss on the leaf, and the end of the line is invented.
invented marginal notes; the margin has only three short notes (ὅρος δικαιοσύνης, ὅρος φρονήσεως, and one more near the foot)
The place names follow a standard Ptolemy list of Egyptian and Palestinian towns instead of what the hand wrote. The 'ἀνατολικὴ' gloss is invented.
χρῆν is not at the start of line 3; the line begins τοὺς γὰρ.
page has ἐνδέχετο, the earlier reading; made identical to the corrected form, so the note no longer makes sense
The white marks in the middle of the leaf are holes and tears in the parchment. The candidate presents them as a decorative cross dividing two sections of text, which the page does not have.
The page has κατεπτηχώς here. The candidate repeats κατηφής from the line above instead.

examples.quote: the voyage of the demigods brought about. They entered the <term>Phasis</term>; there they joined their strength against the terrible-looking <term>Colchians</t
examples.what: The whole body translates the next leaf: it picks up the end of 'sed iam mortem ipsis illa' and goes on to Phasis, the Colchians, the wryneck and Medea. None of that is on this page.
